description:
FIND-1501's fix (iteration 16) is genuinely, completely resolved: `countChildrenProvisioning({ledgerRows})` unambiguously derives `childrenProvisioning` from `ledger.js`'s real, last-write-wins-reduced rows (behavioral-spec.md:759-784, 849-854; verification-architecture.md:171, 174, PROP-102h/PROP-102i at lines 342-343, Gate item (1g) at lines 699-707), REQ-102's real orchestration is bound to call it directly (never a hand-rolled reimplementation), and the four-case fixture (only-provisioning-counted; provisioning-then-active-not-counted; provisioning-then-failed-not-counted; provisioning-then-active-then-bootstrap_failed-not-counted) is unambiguous and mirrors `deriveRecentSpawnAttempts`'s own established pattern exactly. The sweep-found sibling gap (`deriveMeasuredShelterCostUsd`/`shelter-cost-ledger.js`) is likewise genuinely resolved: null-on-empty, else last-appended-entry's `settledLeaseCostUsd`, never avg/max/first, is unambiguously specified (behavioral-spec.md:1883-1899, 2001-2011; verification-architecture.md:172-173, PROP-102j at line 344, and PROP-303c -- confirmed by grep to now correctly cite `deriveMeasuredShelterCostUsd`/`readShelterCostEntries` by name in the Gate at lines 607-612 -- no residual 'unnamed threshold computation' phrasing remains anywhere).

However, this iteration's own mandated task -- independently re-verify that the builder's own claimed 'full-spec sweep' (iteration 16's RESOLUTION-NOTES.md) was ACTUALLY exhaustive, by re-examining every parameter of every pure function in the Purity Boundary Map myself -- surfaces a FOURTH, previously-undetected instance of the IDENTICAL failure class (a pinned pure-function input sourced from real system computation/state, with no named function or binding rule specifying how that value is actually obtained at runtime): REQ-202's own `needsSolanaWallet({ initialSkills, deployTarget }) -> boolean` (behavioral-spec.md:1519; verification-architecture.md:370, PROP-202a).

Two separate, unaddressed gaps in this ONE function's signature:

(a) `deployTarget` -- REQ-202's own EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md:1499-1508) states Solana keypair generation is needed '...OR the child will be deployed via Nosana (REQ-302, which itself requires a Solana-funded wallet...)'. Which cloud target a given spawn attempt actually uses is NOT a fixture/config value -- it is the real, per-attempt output of REQ-306's own dedicated decision function, `selectCloudTarget({nosanaAvailable, nosanaPriceUsd, akashAvailable, akashPriceUsd}) -> "nosana"|"akash"|"none"` (behavioral-spec.md:2293-2347; verification-architecture.md:178), computed via a real, effectful price/availability query immediately before each spawn attempt (REQ-306's own EARS clause: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL query BOTH providers' current price/availability... immediately before each spawn attempt'). Nowhere in either spec file is there a stated rule that REQ-202's real orchestration passes `needsSolanaWallet`'s `deployTarget` argument as the DIRECT return value of THAT SAME attempt's `selectCloudTarget(...)` call -- the exact 'never hand-assembled by the calling orchestration, ALWAYS the direct return value of X()' binding discipline this SAME iteration's own FIND-1501 fix just established for `childrenProvisioning`/`countChildrenProvisioning`, and iteration 15's FIND-1401 fix established for `recentSpawnAttempts`/`deriveRecentSpawnAttempts`. A grep of both spec files for `selectCloudTarget` (10 total occurrences) confirms zero of them bind its output to `needsSolanaWallet`'s `deployTarget` parameter, and REQ-202's own text (behavioral-spec.md:1499-1524) never once mentions REQ-306 supplying this value programmatically -- only prose describing what the parameter conceptually MEANS.

This is not a cosmetic gap: REQ-302's own EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md:1805-1817) is explicit that the Nosana deploy step provisions the child's compute 'pointed at the child's OWN pre-generated, isolated Solana keypair (REQ-202)' -- i.e., REQ-302 structurally REQUIRES that REQ-202 already generated a Solana wallet for this specific child whenever Nosana ends up being the selected target. If `deployTarget` is hand-assembled at the call site (e.g. an implementer guesses/hardcodes a value, or reads a stale/wrong candidate from an earlier evaluation pass rather than THIS attempt's real `selectCloudTarget` result) and diverges from REQ-306's actual real-time selection for that same attempt, one of two concrete failures results: (i) `deployTarget` wrongly indicates non-Nosana while REQ-306 actually selects Nosana for that attempt -> REQ-202 never generates the Solana wallet REQ-302 structurally requires -> the Nosana deploy step has no keypair to point the CLI at, a hard, deploy-breaking failure of the ENTIRE Nosana path, not a cosmetic bug; or (ii) the reverse mismatch wastes a real, billable Solana keygen for a child that will never use it. Exactly the same class of hazard (a naive/incorrect binding at the call site silently breaking a downstream requirement) that FIND-1401/FIND-1501 both closed for their own pinned inputs.

(b) `initialSkills` -- this parameter has NO specified source anywhere in either spec document at all, not even a hint. A full-text search of both files for 'skill set'/'initial skill'/'skills[]' (excluding REQ-202's own two mentions) returns zero other occurrences -- no requirement anywhere states whether a spawned child's initial skill set is a fixed literal default (analogous to `MAX_CONCURRENT_SPAWNS`'s stated default), copied from the initiating/parent citizen's own current skill roster, or an agent-level in-envelope choice per REQ-104's own carve-out ('what the child's initial goal framing/prompt should say' is explicitly named as the agent's own choice, behavioral-spec.md:983-985) -- REQ-104 never says `initialSkills` is that SAME carve-out, so this is a genuine, unstated ambiguity, not merely an implicit consequence of an existing rule.

Every proof obligation touching this function treats both parameters as already-given fixture values, never as outputs requiring a real binding/derivation rule: PROP-202a (verification-architecture.md:370) is a bare three-branch fixture test ('unit test, exhaustive branch coverage of the three trigger conditions') with no PROP-102g/PROP-102i-equivalent proving the real orchestration derives `deployTarget` from that SAME attempt's real `selectCloudTarget` call. The Gate's item (4) (verification-architecture.md:737-746), which is REQ-201-205's own dedicated end-to-end confirmation section, lists PROP-201a/PROP-201b/PROP-202c/PROP-203a/PROP-203b/PROP-204c/PROP-205a/PROP-205b by name but never PROP-202a, and never requires confirming `deployTarget`'s real-derivation binding -- the exact same class of Gate-coverage gap FIND-1501 closed one iteration ago for `childrenProvisioning` (which previously had no Gate item requiring its real-ledger derivation either, until item (1g) was added).

evidence.snippet: REQ-202's full EARS clause, Edge Cases, and Acceptance Criteria for `needsSolanaWallet({ initialSkills, deployTarget }) -> boolean` -- describes WHAT the two parameters conceptually mean but never HOW either is obtained from real system state/computation at the moment this function is actually invoked for a real spawn attempt

REQ-306's full definition of `selectCloudTarget({nosanaAvailable, nosanaPriceUsd, akashAvailable, akashPriceUsd}) -> "nosana"|"akash"|"none"`, including its own EARS clause requiring a fresh price/availability query 'immediately before each spawn attempt' -- this is the real, per-attempt source `deployTarget` should be bound to, but no cross-reference from REQ-202 to this function's return value exists anywhere

REQ-302's own EARS clause: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL provision the child's compute using the Nosana CLI... pointed at the child's OWN pre-generated, isolated Solana keypair (REQ-202)' -- proving REQ-302 structurally depends on REQ-202 having already generated a Solana wallet whenever Nosana is the real selected target, which is exactly why an incorrect/hand-assembled `deployTarget` binding is deploy-breaking, not cosmetic

REQ-104's own carve-out names only 'what the child's initial goal framing/prompt should say' as the agent's own in-envelope choice -- `initialSkills` is never named as this same carve-out anywhere, so its status (fixed default vs. agent choice vs. parent-inherited) remains a genuine, unstated ambiguity

PROP-202a | REQ-202 | `needsSolanaWallet({initialSkills, deployTarget})` returns `true` exactly when a Solana-settled skill OR Nosana deploy target is present, `false` otherwise | 1 | true | unit test, exhaustive branch coverage of the three trigger conditions (Solana skill / Nosana target / neither) -- an already-given fixture-value test; no PROP-102g/PROP-102i-equivalent integration proof exists binding `deployTarget` to a real `selectCloudTarget` call for the SAME attempt

Gate item (4) -- REQ-201-205's own dedicated end-to-end confirmation section -- enumerates PROP-201a, PROP-201b/PROP-202c, PROP-203a, PROP-203b, PROP-201/303's structural checks, PROP-204c, PROP-205a/b by name, but never PROP-202a and never any requirement to confirm `deployTarget`'s real-derivation binding to `selectCloudTarget`'s output for that same attempt

Purity Boundary Map's `selectCloudTarget` row and `gen-solana-wallet.sh`/`needsSolanaWallet` row (implicit, REQ-202) -- neither row cross-references the other; `selectCloudTarget`'s output is never cited as `needsSolanaWallet`'s `deployTarget` input anywhere in this table
